explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/433: with G(A) the Frobenius number and g(k,n) the maximum over k-subsets A ⊆ [1,n] with gcd 1, is g(k,n) ~ n²/(k−1)? Read for fixed k, this was proved by Dixmier. frobeniusNumber is sSup of the complement of the additive submonoid generated by A, which is finite when gcd = 1. When 1 ∈ A the complement is empty and the value is 0 rather than −1, which is irrelevant asymptotically. The statement asserts g(k,n)/(n²/(k−1)) → 1 for every fixed k ≥ 2. Faithful.
